trust_decision.summary: The compiler decides whether a key path from a TOML table header may descend into an existing value. It does this only with string path bookkeeping (valueAssignments) in deepRef, so when that bookkeeping drifts out of sync, the header walks through a scalar or Date into its JS prototype chain and writes onto Object.prototype.

landing_point.why: deepRef is the only function that walks table-header paths ([a.b.c]) and assigns into ctx[key], so a reader looking for __proto__ pollution goes here first.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Every change is inside compile() in lib/compiler.js. The only public API is toml.parse (index.js:5-9).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver may argue that the path-key desync fixes in assign() and addTableArray() (lib/compiler.js:61,77,164-172) are 'just bookkeeping/correctness bugs' and leave them alone once deepRef blocks __proto__ or non-owned descent, or may argue that the Date objects produced by the parser are not tables.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A table literally named __proto__, or a 'constructor' key, must still parse as an own property of the null-prototype result, so a blocklist on '__proto__' / 'constructor' keys breaks legitimate documents.

O6_input_shapes: [table] header descending through a scalar value that was registered under a mismatched path key (multi-segment currentPath stringified as 'a,b')
[table] header after [[array]] prefix-clears valueAssignments for a sibling key sharing the prefix ('aa' cleared by [[a]])
chained __proto__.__proto__ segments, so a single-__proto__ check is insufficient
nested header under polluted path ([...__proto__.__proto__.code]) creating objects on Object.prototype
quoted keys containing '.' (quoteDottedString) used consistently in all path keys
descent into an empty or last element of a table array (fix.diff:152-159)

O7_producer.where: lib/compiler.js:61, lib/compiler.js:77, lib/compiler.js:164-169 (path-key strings recorded in assign/addTableArray and consumed by the deepRef check at lib/compiler.js:196)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: assign() intermediate check accepts any typeof 'object' non-array, including parser-produced Date values (src/toml.pegjs:315), and relies only on valueAssignments; a desync there would let a dotted key walk Date.prototype to Object.prototype
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix added the owned-container check only to deepRef, not to assign or setNestedKey, so a maintainer could plausibly leave the dotted-key path depending on string bookkeeping.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: setNestedKey for inline tables has the same typeof-object test with no ownership check; a Date value inside an inline table could be an intermediate if definedKeys desyncs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same idiom as assign() and was only touched for pathKey quoting.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: quoteDottedString only quotes keys containing '.', so a key containing a quote or the separator in another form can collide in path-key identity
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is a parser differential on the protected item's identity, a how-type sibling, and the fix still relies on this encoding (fix.diff:185-187).

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via key-path bookkeeping desync in a parser/compiler

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject or skip keys named '__proto__' / 'constructor' in deepRef, or stop descent into non-objects. This breaks the [__proto__] own-table behaviour or leaves the path-key desync in assign/addTableArray unfixed.
